text.p: Harcourt General Inc reported first quarter, ended January 31, earnings per share slipped to $0.20 from $0.23 a year ago, saying the decline reflects a larger seasonal loss, as planned, from its publishing operations, lower earnings from its professional services segment and the recognition of expenses associated with the resignation of its former president.

The company said corporate expenses in the first quarter rose to $10.7 million from $7.4 million a year ago due primarily to the recognition of $3.6 million in expenses associated with the resignation in December of Robert J. Tarr.

The company said the larger loss reflects higher spending in the current year by its educational publishing businesses as they prepare for significant adoption opportunities later in the year. The publishing segment typically has operating losses in the first two fiscal quarters, when major selling and marketing expenses associated with the educational businesses are incurred but sales are minimal.
"The publishing loss in the quarter was in line with our expectations," chief executive Richard A. Smith said.

"Based on early reaction from the educational marketplace to our instructional programs and assuming that the STMP and international businesses maintain their momentum, we continue to anticipate that our publishing group will have a strong performance for the full year."

The company's professional services segment, which consists of Drake Beam Morin's outplacement operations, had revenues of $26.2 million in the 1997 first quarter, down from $31.5 million a year earlier. Operating earnings declined to $0.2 million from $3.5 million the previous year.
Smith noted the outplacement industry continues to suffer from a scarcity of large downsizing projects, which has affected the revenue and profitability of Drake.
After taxes, those expenses reduced earnings per share in the quarter by $0.03.
The company also said it purchased 442,000 common shares in open market transactions during the first quarter for about $20.1 million, or an average of about $45.56 per share.

Publishing revenues in the quarter rose 12.1 percent to $198.4 million, led by gains in the scientific, technical, medical, professional (STMP) and International groups. The anticipated seasonal loss from the publishing businesses was $19.5 million in the latest quarter compared with $11.3 million a year ago.
